item: The pinned dataset prints no score at all for 2026 weeks 10-18
detail: 136 of the 272 2026 rows in data/decision-desk/raw/games.csv.gz carry an empty away_score and home_score, including every Week 11 and later fixture. Only weeks 1-9 are scored (136 games).
impact: Any table that treats this file as a complete 2026 feed understates each club by the games it omits; a 32/32 reconciliation is impossible from this file alone.
resolution: This desk appends the 14 official Week 10 finals read today and publishes the gap week by week in data/corpus_coverage.csv. The remaining 121 fixtures are unplayed or unread, and are labelled so.

item: A published capture asked for the Week 11 injury page and served Week 10
detail: data/nfl-desk-6cbf25fa/injury_reads/capture_injuries_2026-11-18.csv (347 rows) records requested_url = https://www.nfl.com/injuries/league/2026/reg11 and source_url = https://www.nfl.com/injuries/league/2026/reg10. It is Week 10 content filed under a Week 11 request.
impact: Any delta that calls this file the Week 11 prior read compares two different weeks and describes page drift as time drift.
resolution: This desk publishes the delta but labels every row with that caveat, and its own read asserts the printed heading "Injuries - WEEK 11".

item: The pinned spread is stored home-favoured POSITIVE, the opposite of the operator print
detail: The stored line correlates +0.431 with the realised home margin (n=7,087). Fitting the model under the opposite assumption gives a mean absolute error of 8.22 points against 3.41 for the stored convention.
impact: A pipeline that treats a negative stored spread as "home favoured" silently inverts every side it originates.
resolution: The convention is measured at every build and published in data/sign_convention.csv; the origination table prints the operator convention and says so on each row.

item: Two clubs are printed with different codes by the operator and the dataset
detail: nfl.com prints LA and AZ; the pinned dataset prints LAR and ARI. Without an alias the 2026 reconciliation splits two clubs into four.
impact: A silent 30/32 reconciliation that looks like a data problem.
resolution: One alias table is applied at load time and published here; the reconciliation is 32/32 with it.

item: Two clubs are printed as "No Injuries Reported" rather than as a table
detail: The official Week 11 page prints that phrase for CIN and WAS. A capture that turns the phrase into a player row produces a phantom injury entry; a capture that drops it produces an empty club.
impact: Club-level counts and any "injury-free" claim depend on which choice the capture made.
resolution: This desk transcribes the phrase as its own marker row (__NO_INJURIES_REPORTED__) and publishes the club as "printed no injuries", never as "zero injuries".

item: Three Lions players print a blank game-status cell on the official page
detail: Kerby Joseph, Cade Mays and D.J. Reed are printed on the Week 11 report with an empty Game Status cell. An earlier desk recorded all three as Out from a separate article. Both can be true; the cell is blank.
impact: Copying the article value into the table would publish a designation the report does not carry.
resolution: The cell stays blank and the three rows are listed here for review.

item: Only one of thirteen venues was read this session
detail: IND at HOU prints HOUSTON, TX / RELIANT STADIUM on the official game centre (read today). The other twelve game centres were not read, so the venue column does not exist in this desk.
impact: A venue-dependent total model would be built on one fixture.
resolution: Left unread and flagged. No venue is inferred from a club name.

item: The intra-day drift table is empty because the earlier capture only covers one game
detail: The 2026-11-19T06:57:28Z capture holds 26 rows (the Thursday game only). Comparing it with the full read at 11:10Z therefore cannot show drift for the other twelve fixtures.
impact: An empty diff here is not evidence that the page was stable.
resolution: The table is published with zero rows and this note; the drift question is recorded as Q01-adjacent work for a full-page capture.

item: One capture stores a page-level phrase in the practice-status field
detail: The 06:57Z capture carries rows whose practice_status reads "No Injuries Reported", i.e. a page statement in a player-level field.
impact: A join on practice status silently treats a phrase as a status.
resolution: Not edited (another session owns the file); recorded here and in Q14.

item: "Played" is measured as "has a snap record", not "was active"
detail: No official inactive list exists in the repository, so the reliability study in data/designation_reliability.csv cannot separate a player who was inactive from one who dressed and never played.
impact: The Questionable play rate is a lower bound on availability.
resolution: Published as a caveat on every row; an official inactive list is the clear condition.

item: "Note" appears as a designation value in the pinned injury data
detail: Six rows in the 2023-2026 pinned files carry report_status "Note", which is not one of the four official designations.
impact: A model that treats the four designations as exhaustive miscodes these six rows.
resolution: Published as its own category with n=6 rather than merged into a designation.

item: Closing prices do not exist yet for any originated market
detail: All 13 Week 11 fixtures kick off after this build, so every closing cell is empty by construction, not by omission.
impact: No CLV, no closing-line skill, and no staking escrow can be computed.
resolution: The closing policy file names the single capture that would fill it.

item: The availability ablation rests on two official designation weeks
detail: Only 2026 week 10 (read 2026-11-12T16:52:39Z) and week 11 (read today) are stamped official sets; every earlier season comes from the pinned dataset.
impact: A negative result on this evidence is about these two weeks.
resolution: Published with the source class of every count in data/availability_counts.csv.

item: Two of the desk's own first numeric passes were wrong and are recorded
detail: (a) the signed spread-to-probability benchmark was first built with an unsigned formula, which made the market benchmark look far worse than the close; (b) the sign convention was first reported as "flipped". Both were caught by measurement and corrected before publication.
impact: Presentation only; the published numbers are the corrected ones.
resolution: The measured sign convention is now a published table and the convention is asserted in verify.py.

item: Twelve of thirteen fixtures have no second-source price cross-check
detail: Both named operators price all 13 fixtures, so the market column is a genuine two-book median; but no independent third source was read to confirm either operator's print.
impact: A mis-transcribed operator price would not be caught by a third party.
resolution: Prices are transcribed verbatim in inputs/ with the read stamp, so a reviewer can diff them against the operator page.
